correctness.rationale: Rank-one SVD A=σu vᵀ reduces the pseudoinverse error to v/σ times e=(uᵀ ΩΩᵀR)/(uᵀΩΩᵀu), with Δ=||e||². For Gaussian Ω, conditioning on its first row gives e_G=(ZᵀR)/sqrt(X), X~χ²_ell, Z standard in u⊥ independent. Haar projection P gives T=uᵀPu~Beta(ell/2,(n−ell)/2), orthogonal projection length sqrt(T(1−T)), independent uniform sphere direction S; hence e_H=sqrt(Y/X)SᵀR with Y~χ²_{n−ell}. Beta–gamma factorization B||Z||²~χ²_{n−ell} and rotation invariance identify the entire joint row-vector law, not merely coordinate marginals. B strictly (0,1) implies all-threshold error stochastic dominance when R≠0. Chi-square small-ball and dominated convergence give exact t^(−ell/2) constants and moment cutoff; rank-deficient d and multiple outputs are handled. Independent beta moment check at n=10,ell=4 gives E B=2/3 and E B²=16/33, matching tail constant 2/11 vs 3/8. No numerical experiment substitutes for distributional proof.

value.rationale: Exact every-threshold reliability and heavy-tail coefficient answer a practical mathematical question not settled by average-error minimax analysis; the independence coupling gives a natural complete rank-one law and improves understanding even when mean errors diverge (ell=2).

final_claim: For any fixed real rank-one least-squares design, 2≤ell<n, arbitrary right-hand sides and an independent Haar n×ell orthonormal or standard Gaussian sketch, the full coefficient-error row satisfies e_H ≍ sqrt(B)e_G for B~Beta((n−ell)/2,(ell−1)/2) independent of e_G. Thus excess errors satisfy Δ_H ≍ BΔ_G, strict tail dominance for nonzero residual, full moment thresholds s<ell/2 and sharp t^(−ell/2) tail constants.
